newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TI-Acer plans T$100 bln Taiwan wafer project.
newsitem.headline: TI-Acer plans T$100 bln Taiwan wafer project.

text.p: TI-Acer, a joint venture of Acer Inc of Taiwan and Texas Instruments Inc, said on Wednesday it would invest T$100 billion to build an eight-inch wafer fabrication plant in Taiwan by 2000.
The wafer facility would be one of the world's most advanced semiconductor plants, the company said in a statement.

TI-Acer said it planned to build 12-inch wafer fabs in Taiwan after 2000 with total investment far exceeding that for the eight-inch facility, but would not unveil details until its parent companies give approval.

The announcement was the third involving major wafermaking plants in as many months, coming fast on the heels of project announcements by Taiwan's number one and two chipmakers, Taiwan Semiconductor and United Microelectronics.
In June, United Microelectronics announced a T$500 billion (US$18 billion), 10-year wafer fabrication project -- Taiwan's single biggest investment scheme to date.
Rival Taiwan Semiconductor said in April it was launching a T$400 billion (US$14 bilion), 10-year wafer fab project.
TI-Acer said its eight-inch wafer project would reach total monthly capacity of over 100,000 pieces.
TI-Acer, one of Taiwan's leading makers of dynamic random access memory chips, is 48 percent owned by Acer and 33.34 owned by Texas Instruments, with the rest held by other investors.
